title: KV cache slow-drain during shard rebalancing leading to cascading evictions - follow-up and remediation plan
creator: Marta Liu
description: During a scheduled capacity shrink of a dedicated shard pool, background drain tasks degraded and KV prefix cache entries were not evicted in a timely, coordinated manner. This produced a cascading eviction wave that caused elevated latency and transient OOMs on a subset of serving nodes. This ticket captures the follow-up actions, short-term mitigations, and long-term hardening work.
impact_summary: The incident lasted ~27 minutes starting 2025-11-03T02:08Z. Approximately 6% of hosted requests experienced >3x token latency; three dedicated GPUs experienced transient OOM restarts causing ~40 minutes of reduced capacity on rotated shards. No customer data was lost; some requests returned 500s and spiky tail latencies affected a handful of mid-size customers with strict latency SLOs.
root_cause_summary: Race between shard rebalancer drain step and the cache compaction/eviction worker. Drain path held a soft lock preventing background compactor from promoting hot items to longer-lived slabs. When drain completed, a large number of short-lived entries became eligible simultaneously, causing eviction comparator thrashing and hashing hotspots; this triggered memory churn and a few allocator fallback conditions leading to OOMs.
timeline_summary:
- 02:07: scheduled drain started (automated scale-down)
- 02:09: background compaction queue latency increased, error rate for compactor retries rose
- 02:10-02:18: eviction scoring oscillated, eviction storms across 3 shards; latency increased
- 02:35: autoscaling rollback and emergency draining pause applied, eviction wave subsided
- 03:05: control plane rebalanced traffic, impacted nodes recovered after restarts
- 03:35: incident declared resolved
Post-incident: on-call created mitigation PR and added emergency guardrail for scale-downs.
action_items: DR-001: Add a coordinated drain barrier that yields to compaction for up to 2s during rebalances to avoid starving background maintenance - owner: Daniel Rivera - due: 2025-11-17
DR-002: Implement batched eviction scoring that applies backpressure rather than performing global immediate evictions - owner: Priya Nambiar - due: 2025-11-24
DR-003: Add a circuit-breaker to abort scale-down drain if compactor queue depth exceeds threshold (observability + kill-switch) - owner: Omar Patel - due: 2025-11-12
DR-004: Introduce a light-weight preflight that simulates post-drain evict set size and blocks drain if predicted eviction volume > X - owner: Linh Tran - due: 2025-12-01
DR-005: Improve allocator telemetry and add slab-level histograms to detect sudden eviction waves earlier - owner: Aisha Khan - due: 2025-11-14
DR-006: Backfill unit + fuzz tests that recreate concurrent drain + compaction races in CI and on a nightly stress job - owner: QA Team (lead: Marco Silva) - due: 2025-11-21
DR-007: Short-term mitigation: block automatic scale-downs for high-throughput shards for 48 hours post-deploys and add an emergency rollout policy - owner: SRE - due: 2025-11-04
qa_validation_plan: Nightly stress job will run a synthetic rebalancing workload that executes 10k drains with randomized compaction timing. Pass criteria: no OOM, no >2x tail latency regression, compactor queue depth stays below critical threshold. Create a dashboard panel to visualize eviction score distribution during runs.
monitoring_changes:
- New metric: kvcache.eviction_wave_count (counter)
- Alert: evictions_per_min > 10k AND compactor_queue_depth > 100 for 2m -> P0 pager
- Dashboard: slab histogram, compactor queue, drain-block-time, per-shard memory headroom
- Log: sample eviction key hashes at 0.1% for post-incident correlation
comments: Priya Nambiar (2025-11-04): Reviewed DR-002; we should prototype batched scoring with probabilistic sampling to reduce scan cost.
Omar Patel (2025-11-05): Added dependency on ENH-4321 (allocator-minor-compact) to avoid duplicate work; flagged potential perf regression risk.
SRE (2025-11-06): Short-term mitigation applied and tested on staging; no regressions observed in 12h smoke run.
Marta Liu (2025-11-07): PM asks for cadence: weekly sync until all DR-* items closed; assigned postmortem owner for customer communications.
notes: This incident highlights an operational class of bugs where background maintenance is implicitly assumed to always make forward progress during control-plane operations. The fix set includes both coordination primitives (barrier/kill-switch) and algorithmic hardening (batched eviction scoring, preflight simulation). Prioritize low-risk telemetry + guardrail items first.
